about.title: Encinitas Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: When a fatal crash happens in Encinitas, the aftermath is disorienting. San Diego County records show traffic deaths occur here every year, often tied to busy corridors like Encinitas Boulevard, N El Camino Real, and I-5, or during the Friday afternoon window when reported collisions tend to cluster. For families left behind, California law recognizes a wrongful death claim as a separate civil action from any criminal proceeding, one built to address the financial and emotional toll of losing a loved one. We handle wrongful death claims directly and can help you sort out who qualifies to bring a claim, what evidence matters, and what deadlines apply. You don't have to figure this out alone, and there's no cost to start the conversation.

items.title: Standing Rules Are Specific
items.desc: California limits who can file a wrongful death claim, generally a spouse, domestic partner, or children first, with other dependents or heirs eligible in certain situations. We can clarify where your family fits.

items.title: The Clock Is Running
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims in California must be filed within two years of the date of death, though claims against a government entity carry a much shorter window. Missing these deadlines can end a claim before it starts.

items.title: Losses Go Beyond Bills
items.desc: California law allows recovery for tangible costs like funeral expenses and lost income, plus non-economic losses such as the loss of a loved one's companionship and guidance. We can help document both.

items.question: How long do we have to file a wrongful death claim in Encinitas?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of death to file, though claims involving a government entity or agency require much faster action, sometimes just months. Because the deadline can vary based on who's responsible, it's worth speaking with us early rather than waiting.

items.question: Does the I-5 corridor through Encinitas affect our claim?
items.answer: Where a fatal crash occurred can matter for evidence collection and jurisdiction, but it doesn't change the core legal standards for a wrongful death claim. We can review the specific circumstances of the crash, whether it happened on I-5, Encinitas Boulevard, or elsewhere, and explain how that location factors into building your case.

items.question: Who is allowed to bring a wrongful death claim under California law?
items.answer: Typically, a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children have the first right to file. If none of those relatives exist, other dependents or heirs may be eligible depending on the family's circumstances. We can help determine exactly who qualifies in your situation.
